jobs.title: Senior Director of Development, CHHS - Search Firm
jobs.description:
Join the vibrant community at California State University, Long Beach (CSULB)!

Located just three miles from the Pacific Ocean, CSULB offers an inspiring workplace and an exceptional Southern California lifestyle. Our 322-acre campus—one of the largest in the CSU system—serves more than 42,000 students and is known for its commitment to student success, innovation, and impactful academic and research initiatives.

As a member of the CSULB community, you’ll experience a dynamic environment filled with cultural landmarks, collaborative energy, and opportunities to make a meaningful difference.

Work-life balance thrives here. Long Beach blends coastal relaxation with urban vibrancy, offering miles of beaches, year-round sunshine, a thriving arts and food scene, and convenient access to both Los Angeles and Orange County. It’s an ideal place to grow your career while enjoying everything Southern California has to offer.

Join the California State University (CSU) and explore career opportunities that advance student success and strengthen California’s future—offering competitive compensation, comprehensive benefits, and professional growth.

Job Summary

The Senior Director of Development for the College of Health and Human Services (CHHS) is responsible for securing major gifts of $25,000+ with a focus on gifts above $100,000 including principal gifts at $1 million+ in support of the university, with an emphasis on CHHS.

Reporting to the Associate Vice President for Development, this role partners closely with the college dean and faculty to provide strategic leadership, increasing both the number and size of major and principal gifts. The position assesses philanthropic priorities and aligns them with prospective donors to benefit the college and university.

The Senior Director serves as the primary development officer, leading donor identification, prospecting, cultivation, solicitation, stewardship, and communication for gifts exceeding $100,000. The Senior Director manages the full donor lifecycle while building and sustaining strong relationships between the university and its benefactors, advancing a culture of philanthropy across major, principal, and planned giving.

Key Responsibilities

Identify, cultivate, and solicit major gifts of $25,000+ with a focus on gifts above $100,000 including principal gifts at $1 million+ from individuals, corporations and foundations to support CHHS and university.
Facilitate university-wide collaboration amongst corporate and foundation donors that support multiple colleges.
Manage strategic volunteer development opportunities for major gift prospects.
Collaborate with URD (VP and AVP, Development) and the dean of the College of Health and Human Services to identify college philanthropic priorities and create successful development strategies for each one.
Write such materials (e.g., proposals, gift agreements) as are necessary for the fund-raising tasks.

Department

University Development

Duration of Appointment

This is a regular, at-will position.

Classification

Administrator II

Compensation

Salary placement is determined by the education, experience, and qualifications the candidate brings to the position, internal equity, and the hiring department’s fiscal resources.

CSU MPP Compensation Summary Range: The MPP Comp Summary Range for this position is $10,069 - $15,104 per month.

Benefits

At California State University (CSU), we prioritize the health, growth, and success of our employees. Our benefits program reflects our commitment to your overall well-being.

To Be Eligible For Full Benefits, Employees Must Be Appointed At Least Half-time (.50 FTE) With An Appointment Lasting More Than Six Months And One Day. Benefits Eligibility And Offerings May Vary Based On Appointment Type, Classification, And Applicable Collective Bargaining Agreement. Eligible Employees May Have Access To a Comprehensive Benefits Package That Can Include:

Paid Time Off: Up to 24 vacation days per year (based on employee group and/or length of service), 14 paid holidays, and 12 sick days annually with unlimited accrual.
Health Coverage: A variety of medical, dental, and vision plans.
Retirement Plans: Participation in the CalPERS defined benefit plan, along with voluntary savings options such as 403(b), 401(k), and 457 plans.
Educational Benefits: Tuition fee waiver programs for eligible employees; dependent eligibility varies by employee group and bargaining unit.
Employee Assistance Program (EAP): Confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.
Additional Benefits: Wellness programs, professional development opportunities, and insurance options including life, disability, and pet insurance.

Candidates are encouraged to review the appropriate CSU Employee Benefits Summary for details specific to their position. Additionally, the CSU Total Compensation Calculator is available to help prospective employees understand the full value of the CSU benefits package and how it complements base salary.

Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

The ideal candidate brings strong knowledge of the solicitation process within an educational environment and demonstrates a proven ability to identify, cultivate, and build a pipeline of future donors. They are skilled in partnering with college leadership to establish major and principal gift priorities and develop effective strategies to achieve fundraising success. This individual possesses excellent planning, organizational, and problem-solving abilities, along with strong oral and written communication skills. They are effective supervisors, capable of leading and managing a college development office and its staff, while also working independently with minimal oversight. A high degree of self-direction is essential, as they must be able to initiate, coordinate, and successfully complete tasks with accountability and efficiency.

Ability to communicate with an ethnically and culturally diverse campus community. Ability to follow all university policies, procedures, and guidelines including but not limited to safety, civility, information security, and non-discrimination policies and procedures. Ability to contribute to a positive university experience for each and every student and assist in achieving the university's commitment to a "vision of excellence."

Education And Experience

Bachelor's degree and 7 years of demonstrated successful major gift fundraising experience including donor identification, cultivation, and solicitation.
Experience in higher education preferred.

Licenses / Certificates

Valid California driver's license required.

Employees who are required to operate motorized vehicles and/or use their personal vehicle more than once a month on university business are required to take a mandatory Defensive Driving course and enroll in the DMV Employee Pull Notice (EPN) Program.

Application Procedures

Another Source has been retained for this search. To ensure your application is received please apply directly through Another Source candidate portal by clicking here.

Please fill out the application completely. It is important that all sections of the online application are completed fully and accurately. Be sure to include all relevant education and experience. Your application will be used to determine whether you meet the minimum qualifications for this position.

Physical Summary

Sedentary work
- Involves mainly sitting. Walking and standing are minimal. Lifting is limited to lightweight objects (10 pounds or less).

Additional Information

CSULB is not a sponsoring agency for staff and management positions (i.e. H-1B Visas).

A background check (including a criminal records check) must be completed satisfactorily and is required for employment. CSULB will make a conditional offer of employment, which may be rescinded if the background check reveals disqualifying information, and/or it is discovered that the candidate knowingly withheld or falsified information. Failure to satisfactorily complete the background check may affect the continued employment of a current CSU employee who was conditionally offered the position.

Due to the nature of this position, current CSULB employees are subject to a criminal record check unless they have successfully completed a criminal background check through CSULB within the past 12 months.

The person holding this position is considered a 'mandated reporter' under the California Child Abuse and Neglect Reporting Act and is required to comply with the requirements set forth in CSU Executive Order 1083 Revised July 21, 2017 as a condition of employment.

The duties of this position will include participation in decisions that may have a material financial benefit to the incumbent. Therefore, the selected candidate will be required to file Conflict of Interest Form 700: Statement of Economic Interest on an annual basis, complete ethics training within 6 months of appointment, and attend this training every other year thereafter.

jobs.description:
Description

The Osborne Association serves individuals, families, and communities affected by the criminal justice system. Through our programs, we offer opportunities for people to heal from and repair harm, restore their lives, and thrive. We challenge systems rooted in racism and retribution and fight for policies and practices that promote true safety, justice, and liberation.

At Osborne, we are guided by core values and shared beliefs. We honor everyone's capacity to change, celebrate our shared humanity, are united in our pursuit of justice and equity, take all possible steps to keep our commitments, and advocate for people and principles with fierce and tenacious determination.

We currently seek a full-time Deputy Director to join our Workforce Development team. Reporting out of our Brooklyn office, the Deputy Director of Workforce Development will play a key role in designing, implementing, and overseeing strategies to enhance Workforce Development programming. They will collaborate with internal and external stakeholders to leverage resources, build partnerships, and expand workforce opportunities. Additionally, the Deputy Director will ensure all program contractual obligations are met and provide supervision to direct support staff.

Salary:
$80,000 - $85,000 annually

Essential Duties

Provide direct supervision, coaching, and performance management to the Workforce Unit's Brooklyn Site Coordinator, LGBTQIA+ Case Management Program Coordinator, and CASES Career Coach, ensuring high-quality service delivery, staff accountability, and achievement of program goals.
Lead the coordination, implementation, and oversight of Workforce Development programs by providing staff with ongoing training, technical assistance, guidance, and support to ensure effective service delivery and adherence to organizational policies and funder requirements.
Develop, coordinate, and oversee recruitment, outreach, and engagement strategies to maximize participant enrollment, strengthen community partnerships, and increase program participation.
Monitor program performance through the collection, analysis, and evaluation of program data, identifying trends and implementing continuous quality improvement initiatives to enhance participant outcomes and program effectiveness.
Review, prepare and submit timely program reports, performance updates, and operational analyses to the Workforce Development Director, highlighting accomplishments, challenges, compliance status, and recommendations for improvement.
Coordinate and oversee the implementation of industry-recognized workforce training programs, including but not limited to OSHA, Site Safety Training (SST), Food Protection, and other credentialing opportunities, ensuring compliance with contractual deliverables, participant eligibility requirements, and certification standards.
Build, strengthen, and maintain collaborative relationships with funders, employers, community-based organizations, training providers, government agencies, and other key stakeholders to support program growth, participant success, and long-term sustainability.
Plan, coordinate, and facilitate regular staff meetings, individual supervision sessions, case conferences, and cross-functional planning meetings, implementing corrective actions, coaching strategies, and operational improvements as necessary.
Collaborate closely with internal departments, including Fiscal, Human Resources, Data and Evaluation, Compliance, Development, and Program Operations, to ensure seamless coordination of services and alignment with organizational priorities and strategic initiatives.
Conduct monthly program audits and quality assurance reviews to ensure compliance with organizational policies, contractual obligations, regulatory requirements, documentation standards, and best practices, while developing corrective action plans when necessary.
Coordinate and manage Workforce Development graduation ceremonies and recognition events, including developing the event "Run of Show," coordinating invitations for graduates, guest speakers, employers, funders, and internal/external stakeholders, overseeing event logistics, and ensuring successful execution of all event-related activities.
Oversee the request, inventory, distribution, and closeout of participant support goods, including OMNY cards, gift cards, and other approved incentives, ensuring fiscal accountability and compliance with organizational and funder requirements.
Ensure the timely and accurate documentation of participant support goods in the Electronic Case Management (ECM) system to support compliance, reporting, and audit readiness.
Ensure program operations consistently reflect the organization's mission, values, and strategic objectives while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, equity, and participant-centered service delivery.
In-person attendance is required to collaborate with co-workers
Perform other duties as assigned

Requirements

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s Degree in Criminal Justice, Public Administration or related field with three to five years of progressively responsible program management experience; in lieu of a degree High Diploma or equivalent required with at least 5 years of experience supporting a social service agency in a supervisory capacity.
Masters Degree in social work or related fields strongly preferred.
Experience creating processes that enhance program performance
Knowledge of workforce development and experience supporting criminal justice impacted individuals
Experience managing both performance-based contracts and cost reimbursement contracts preferred

Key Competencies

Strong analytical skills with the ability to collect, organize, analyze, and disseminate large amounts of data while succinctly summarizing conclusions to leadership and key stakeholders
Ability to work effectively under tight deadlines, strong attention to detail, and time management skills
Ability to work in teams and collaborate effectively with people in different functions
Ability to take the initiative and drive for results
Ability to communicate with all levels of the organization and build strong relationships
Proficiency in Microsoft Office, Google Suite, and case management software (i.e.: Salesforce, nFORM)
Strong verbal and written communication skills
Effective decision-making skills
Knowledge and understanding of the various workforce sectors
Knowledge and understanding of government contracts
Experience working with criminal justice involved individuals
Interpersonal and problem resolution skills
Strong supervisory skills

Benefits Of Working At Osborne

Generous benefits include four weeks of vacation, tuition reimbursement, a flexible work schedule, excellent Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance, and a 403(b) plan with a company match. Career development through ongoing training and individual development plans.

The Osborne Association is an EEO/Affirmative Action employer and a VEVRAA Federal Contractor. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment and will not be discriminated against based on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, protected veteran status, unemployment status, or any other protected category. The Osborne Association takes affirmative action in support of its policy to advance in employment individuals who are minorities, women, protected veterans, and individuals with disabilities.

Thank you for your interest in the Osborne Association. Be sure to include a cover letter with your application. No phone calls please. We wish we could personally respond to each application. However, we are unable to do so due to the volume of interest received.

Salary is based on commensurate experience and other qualifications.

At BNY, our culture empowers you to grow and succeed. As a leading global financial services company at the center of the world’s financial system we touch nearly 20% of the world’s investible assets. The role serves as a critical partner to the Head of Engineering and leadership team, helping define direction, improve organizational effectiveness, and ensure the engineering franchise operates with clarity, discipline, and scale.

The role is central to building the operating model, management discipline, and enterprise connectivity needed to scale a more effective, data-driven, and forward-looking Engineering organization.

jobs.description:
Work for Indiana

Begin a fulfilling career with the State of Indiana by joining one of the largest employers in the state, offering a range of opportunities across 60+ agencies. At the state, you'll find competitive compensation, a robust benefits package and a commitment to work-life balance. Most importantly, you'll have the chance to make a real and measurable impact on the lives of Hoosiers across Indiana.

About The Indiana Law Enforcement Training Board

The Indiana Law Enforcement Training Board is the governing body of the Indiana Law Enforcement Academy, located in Plainfield, Indiana. The Board is comprised of 17 members, who have been appointed by the governor. The board sets the requirements and criteria for the basic training of law enforcement officers throughout the State of Indiana, which became mandatory in 1972.

Role Overview

This position serves as agency head for the Indiana Law Enforcement Academy consisting of approximately 60 employees, facilities and over 300 acres of property. Incumbent is also chief administrative officer for the Indiana Law Enforcement Academy/Law Enforcement Training Board and serves as the chief of ILEA Police Department. This is a complex executive, leadership, management and administrative position requiring significant executive depth.

Position Incumbent has the responsibility for overseeing and establishing the development of basic training for:

Police recruits.
Continuing education.
Advanced training and regional training programs for all law enforcement officers throughout the state, as well as leaders, managers and executives in law enforcement.

Incumbent works with the LETB to set statewide policies for fitness, use of force, vehicle pursuits, defensive tactics and any and all high liability police activity.

Salary

The University of Miami is seeking an experienced leader to direct physician and faculty compensation strategy, ensuring competitive, compliant, and market-aligned programs across the academic medical enterprise.

The Executive Director, Physician & Faculty Compensation leads the strategy, design, and administration of compensation programs for physicians and faculty within an academic medical center environment.

This role is responsible for ensuring all compensation arrangements are fair market value (FMV), commercially reasonable, and compliant with applicable federal and state regulations, including Stark Law and Anti-Kickback Statute requirements.

The Executive Director partners closely with clinical, academic, and administrative leadership to develop productivity-based and mission-driven compensation models that support organizational goals related to patient care, research, education, and financial performance. This role also oversees faculty compensation governance processes, contract administration, and market benchmarking, while monitoring industry trends to inform compensation strategies.

Core Job Functions

Compensation Strategy & Governance

Leads the design, implementation, and ongoing evaluation of physician and faculty compensation models, including base salary, productivity incentives (e.g., wRVUs), quality metrics, and academic incentives.
Partners with the Compensation Committee and executive leadership to ensure alignment with institutional strategy and market practices.
Collaborates closely with Compliance, Finance, Human Resources, and Clinical Operations teams on compensation-related matters.
Builds strong relationships with academic and clinical leadership to ensure transparency and understanding of compensation models.
Prepares and presents compensation analyses and recommendations to senior leadership and governing bodies.
Ensures all compensation arrangements are supported by documented FMV and commercial reasonableness analyses.
Maintains compliance with all applicable regulatory requirements, including Stark Law, Anti-Kickback Statute, and IRS guidelines for tax-exempt organizations.
Establishes and monitors internal controls and audit processes related to physician and faculty compensation programs

Market Benchmarking & Analytics

Oversees market benchmarking using national compensation surveys (e.g., MGMA, AAMC, SullivanCotter) to inform compensation structures and pay decisions.
Provides advanced analytics related to productivity (wRVUs), compensation per wRVU, collections, and performance trends by specialty and provider.
Identifies emerging market trends and provides strategic recommendations to leadership.
Partners with Department Chairs, Vice Chairs, and the Dean’s Office to develop and implement specialty-specific compensation plans aligned with clinical, academic, and research expectations.
Supports recruitment and retention efforts through development of competitive compensation packages, including start-up funding and ramp-up models.
Provides historical performance and productivity data to inform recruitment and compensation plan design.

Financial Planning & Documentation

Oversees the administration and lifecycle management of all physician and faculty employment agreements, including initial contracts, amendments, and renewals.
Ensures accurate and complete documentation of compensation terms, incentive plans, and supporting FMV analyses.
Develops and manages compensation budget guidelines, including forecasting physician and faculty compensation costs based on productivity and growth projections.
Supports business planning efforts through modeling of compensation scenarios and financial impact analyses.

Data/Systems Management & Reporting

Leads the development and standardization of compensation data infrastructure to ensure accuracy, consistency, and accessibility across departments.
Oversees reporting frameworks and dashboards related to compensation, productivity, and financial performance.
Ensures effective data governance and integration across systems supporting physician and faculty compensation.
Defines business requirements and leads the implementation and ongoing enhancement of systems supporting physician compensation (e.g., reporting tools, compensation management systems).
Oversees testing, validation, and maintenance of compensation-related systems and reporting tools.
Develops educational resources and training for leaders and staff on compensation programs and processes.
Establishes and continuously assesses the effectiveness of the internal controls within the unit and compliance with University policies and procedures. Ensures employees are trained on controls within the function and on University policy and procedures.

Strategic Alignment: Skilled in aligning departmental goals with enterprise-wide strategy and develops comprehensive strategic plans.

Position Overview

The Director of Operations & Administration is responsible for overseeing the day-to-day administrative and operational functions of a recreational sports club serving approximately 1,000 participants and their families
.
This individual will be the central point of coordination for registrations, scheduling, parent communication, coaches, facilities, payments, uniforms/equipment, vendors, events, and general club administration.
The ideal candidate is extremely organized, responsive, detail-oriented, and comfortable managing a high volume of families, coaches, schedules, and operational issues simultaneously.
The primary objective of this position is simple: make sure the club runs smoothly and provide families and coaches with an excellent experience.

Key Responsibilities

Registration & Participant Administration

Manage registration for approximately 1,000 participants.
Maintain accurate participant, family, team, and coach records.
Manage registration platforms and club databases.
Track registrations, payments, waivers, required forms, and outstanding balances.
Coordinate roster creation and participant placement.
Manage waitlists, late registrations, cancellations, refunds, and registration changes.
Maintain accurate contact information and participant records.

Parent & Customer Service

Serve as the primary administrative resource for club families.
Responsibilities include:
Responding to parent questions and concerns.
Providing information regarding schedules, locations, registrations, payments, uniforms, and club policies.
Managing the club’s primary administrative email accounts.
Creating consistent communication processes so families receive timely information.
Escalating significant issues to club leadership when necessary.
Maintaining a professional and customer-service-oriented relationship with families.

Team & Coach Administration

Maintain coach and volunteer databases.
Coordinate coach registration and onboarding.
Track required certifications, background checks, and documentation.
Distribute team rosters and relevant operational information.
Maintain coach contact lists.
Communicate schedules, policies, deadlines, and club updates to coaches.
Serve as the administrative liaison between coaches and club leadership.
Assist with recruiting and organizing volunteer coaches when necessary.

Scheduling & Facilities

Own the administrative coordination of club schedules and facilities.
Responsibilities include:
Practice scheduling.
Game scheduling and coordination.
Field/facility assignments.
Facility calendars.
Weather-related changes.
Cancellations and rescheduling.
Communication of schedule changes to coaches and families.
Coordination with municipalities, schools, facility operators, and other field providers.
Tracking facility agreements and usage.

The Director should maintain a centralized operating calendar so leadership always has visibility into club activities.
Financial Administration

Work with club leadership and bookkeeping/accounting resources to manage basic financial administration.
Responsibilities include:
Tracking participant payments.
Monitoring outstanding balances.
Processing approved refunds and credits.
Managing payment plans.
Maintaining vendor invoices.
Coordinating vendor payments.
Tracking facility expenses.
Maintaining organized financial documentation.
Assisting with budget preparation and expense tracking.
Providing regular registration and revenue reports to leadership.

This position is not necessarily responsible for performing the organization’s accounting but should ensure that financial information is organized, accurate, and delivered to the appropriate accounting resources.
Uniforms, Equipment & Inventory

Coordinate uniform ordering and distribution.
Manage relationships with apparel and equipment vendors.
Maintain inventory of club equipment and supplies.
Track equipment issued to teams and coaches.
Coordinate equipment pickup and return.
Identify equipment needs before each season.
Ensure teams have necessary equipment prior to practices and games.

Seasonal Operations

Develop and manage a detailed operational calendar for each season.
This includes:
Pre-Season

Registration
Coach recruitment
Background checks
Team formation
Scheduling
Facility assignments
Uniform ordering
Equipment distribution
Parent communication
Coach communication

During the Season

Schedule management
Weather communication
Parent support
Coach support
Registration changes
Facility coordination
Equipment needs
Operational troubleshooting

Post-Season

Equipment collection
Financial reconciliation
Family surveys
Coach feedback
Registration reporting
Vendor reconciliation
Operational review
Recommendations for the following season

Technology & Systems

Manage and maintain the administrative systems used by the organization, which may include:
Registration software
Team-management applications
Scheduling software
Email systems
Website administration
Payment-processing platforms
QuickBooks or similar accounting systems
Google Workspace / Microsoft Office
Shared files and club databases

The Director should continually identify opportunities to automate repetitive administrative work and improve efficiency.
Policies & Risk Administration

Maintain participant waivers and required documentation.
Coordinate background checks and coach requirements.
Maintain insurance certificates and facility documentation.
Maintain organized electronic club records.
Assist leadership with implementing club policies and procedures.
Ensure administrative processes are consistently followed.

Events & Club Programming

Provide operational support for:
Opening-day events
Clinics
Camps
Tournaments
Picture days
Parent meetings
Coach meetings
Fundraising events
Community events
End-of-season activities

Leadership & Operational Management

The Director of Operations & Administration should operate as the central operational hub of the organization
.
Rather than leadership becoming involved in every scheduling issue, parent question, payment problem, uniform issue, or coach request, this individual should own those processes and escalate only issues requiring leadership decisions.
The Director will also help establish documented processes and operating procedures so the organization can continue to grow without creating unnecessary administrative complexity.
Key Performance Indicators

Performance should be measured using clear operational standards, including:
Registration accuracy
Response time to parent inquiries
Payment collection rate
Scheduling accuracy
Coach onboarding completion
Background-check compliance
Uniform delivery accuracy
Facility utilization
Number of unresolved parent/coach issues
Administrative cost per participant
Family satisfaction
Coach satisfaction

Qualifications

The ideal candidate will have:
3–5+ years of operations, administration, customer service, event management, or sports-management experience.
Strong organizational and project-management skills.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to manage hundreds of families and multiple teams simultaneously.
Strong attention to detail.
Experience working with registration or scheduling software.
Comfort working with spreadsheets, databases, and financial information.
Strong customer-service skills.
Ability to solve problems independently.
Willingness to work occasional evenings and weekends during peak periods.
Youth sports or recreational sports experience preferred.

Ideal Candidate Profile

We are looking for someone who is a highly organized operator and problem solver
.
This person should enjoy creating structure, building systems, communicating with families, and making sure hundreds of small operational details are completed correctly and on time.
They should be comfortable taking ownership rather than waiting for direction.
The successful candidate will constantly ask:
“What needs to happen next, who owns it, and how do we make sure it gets done?”

What Success Looks Like

Within the first year, this individual should create an operating environment where:
Families know exactly where to go for information.
Parent inquiries are answered quickly.
Coaches receive clear and timely communication.
Registrations and payments are accurately tracked.
Teams and schedules are organized well in advance.
Facilities are properly coordinated.
Uniforms and equipment arrive on time.
Leadership has accurate operational and financial reporting.
Administrative problems are solved before they become leadership problems.
The club has documented systems that can support continued growth beyond 1,000 participants.

Ultimately, the Director of Operations & Administration should allow club leadership to focus on strategy, programming, coaching quality, growth, partnerships, and the long-term direction of the organization
while this position owns the operational execution required to keep the club running successfully.

The Indiana Law Enforcement Training Board is the governing body of the Indiana Law Enforcement Academy, located in Plainfield, Indiana. The board sets the requirements and criteria for the basic training of law enforcement officers throughout the State of Indiana, which became mandatory in 1972.

This position serves as agency head for the Indiana Law Enforcement Academy consisting of approximately 60 employees, facilities and over 300 acres of property. Incumbent is also chief administrative officer for the Indiana Law Enforcement Academy/Law Enforcement Training Board and serves as the chief of ILEA Police Department. This is a complex executive, leadership, management and administrative position requiring significant executive depth.

Position Incumbent has the responsibility for overseeing and establishing the development of basic training for:

Police recruits.
Continuing education.
Advanced training and regional training programs for all law enforcement officers throughout the state, as well as leaders, managers and executives in law enforcement.

Incumbent works with the LETB to set statewide policies for fitness, use of force, vehicle pursuits, defensive tactics and any and all high liability police activity.

to view the total compensation package.

Serves as Executive Director for Indiana Law Enforcement Academy/Law Enforcement Training Board;

Establishes policy for the daily operation of the ILEA facility in Plainfield, Indiana.

The University of Miami is seeking an experienced leader to direct physician and faculty compensation strategy, ensuring competitive, compliant, and market-aligned programs across the academic medical enterprise.

The Executive Director, Physician & Faculty Compensation leads the strategy, design, and administration of compensation programs for physicians and faculty within an academic medical center environment.

This role is responsible for ensuring all compensation arrangements are fair market value (FMV), commercially reasonable, and compliant with applicable federal and state regulations, including Stark Law and Anti-Kickback Statute requirements.

The Executive Director partners closely with clinical, academic, and administrative leadership to develop productivity-based and mission-driven compensation models that support organizational goals related to patient care, research, education, and financial performance. This role also oversees faculty compensation governance processes, contract administration, and market benchmarking, while monitoring industry trends to inform compensation strategies.

Core Job Functions

Compensation Strategy & Governance

Leads the design, implementation, and ongoing evaluation of physician and faculty compensation models, including base salary, productivity incentives (e.g., wRVUs), quality metrics, and academic incentives.
Partners with the Compensation Committee and executive leadership to ensure alignment with institutional strategy and market practices.
Collaborates closely with Compliance, Finance, Human Resources, and Clinical Operations teams on compensation-related matters.
Builds strong relationships with academic and clinical leadership to ensure transparency and understanding of compensation models.
Prepares and presents compensation analyses and recommendations to senior leadership and governing bodies.
Ensures all compensation arrangements are supported by documented FMV and commercial reasonableness analyses.
Maintains compliance with all applicable regulatory requirements, including Stark Law, Anti-Kickback Statute, and IRS guidelines for tax-exempt organizations.
Establishes and monitors internal controls and audit processes related to physician and faculty compensation programs

Market Benchmarking & Analytics

Oversees market benchmarking using national compensation surveys (e.g., MGMA, AAMC, SullivanCotter) to inform compensation structures and pay decisions.
Provides advanced analytics related to productivity (wRVUs), compensation per wRVU, collections, and performance trends by specialty and provider.
Identifies emerging market trends and provides strategic recommendations to leadership.
Partners with Department Chairs, Vice Chairs, and the Dean’s Office to develop and implement specialty-specific compensation plans aligned with clinical, academic, and research expectations.
Supports recruitment and retention efforts through development of competitive compensation packages, including start-up funding and ramp-up models.
Provides historical performance and productivity data to inform recruitment and compensation plan design.

Financial Planning & Documentation

Oversees the administration and lifecycle management of all physician and faculty employment agreements, including initial contracts, amendments, and renewals.
Ensures accurate and complete documentation of compensation terms, incentive plans, and supporting FMV analyses.
Develops and manages compensation budget guidelines, including forecasting physician and faculty compensation costs based on productivity and growth projections.
Supports business planning efforts through modeling of compensation scenarios and financial impact analyses.

Data/Systems Management & Reporting

Leads the development and standardization of compensation data infrastructure to ensure accuracy, consistency, and accessibility across departments.
Oversees reporting frameworks and dashboards related to compensation, productivity, and financial performance.
Ensures effective data governance and integration across systems supporting physician and faculty compensation.
Defines business requirements and leads the implementation and ongoing enhancement of systems supporting physician compensation (e.g., reporting tools, compensation management systems).
Oversees testing, validation, and maintenance of compensation-related systems and reporting tools.
Develops educational resources and training for leaders and staff on compensation programs and processes.
Establishes and continuously assesses the effectiveness of the internal controls within the unit and compliance with University policies and procedures. Ensures employees are trained on controls within the function and on University policy and procedures.

Strategic Alignment: Skilled in aligning departmental goals with enterprise-wide strategy and develops comprehensive strategic plans.

Position:

Position Overview

The Director of Operations & Administration is responsible for overseeing the day-to-day administrative and operational functions of a recreational sports club serving approximately 1,000 participants and their families
.
This individual will be the central point of coordination for registrations, scheduling, parent communication, coaches, facilities, payments, uniforms/equipment, vendors, events, and general club administration.
The ideal candidate is extremely organized, responsive, detail-oriented, and comfortable managing a high volume of families, coaches, schedules, and operational issues simultaneously.
The primary objective of this position is simple: make sure the club runs smoothly and provide families and coaches with an excellent experience.

Key Responsibilities

Registration & Participant Administration

Manage registration for approximately 1,000 participants.
Maintain accurate participant, family, team, and coach records.
Manage registration platforms and club databases.
Track registrations, payments, waivers, required forms, and outstanding balances.
Coordinate roster creation and participant placement.
Manage waitlists, late registrations, cancellations, refunds, and registration changes.
Maintain accurate contact information and participant records.

Parent & Customer Service

Serve as the primary administrative resource for club families.
Responsibilities include:
Responding to parent questions and concerns.
Providing information regarding schedules, locations, registrations, payments, uniforms, and club policies.
Managing the club’s primary administrative email accounts.
Creating consistent communication processes so families receive timely information.
Escalating significant issues to club leadership when necessary.
Maintaining a professional and customer-service-oriented relationship with families.

Team & Coach Administration

Maintain coach and volunteer databases.
Coordinate coach registration and onboarding.
Track required certifications, background checks, and documentation.
Distribute team rosters and relevant operational information.
Maintain coach contact lists.
Communicate schedules, policies, deadlines, and club updates to coaches.
Serve as the administrative liaison between coaches and club leadership.
Assist with recruiting and organizing volunteer coaches when necessary.

Scheduling & Facilities

Own the administrative coordination of club schedules and facilities.
Responsibilities include:
Practice scheduling.
Game scheduling and coordination.
Field/facility assignments.
Facility calendars.
Weather-related changes.
Cancellations and rescheduling.
Communication of schedule changes to coaches and families.
Coordination with municipalities, schools, facility operators, and other field providers.
Tracking facility agreements and usage.

The Director should maintain a centralized operating calendar so leadership always has visibility into club activities.
Financial Administration

Work with club leadership and bookkeeping/accounting resources to manage basic financial administration.
Responsibilities include:
Tracking participant payments.
Monitoring outstanding balances.
Processing approved refunds and credits.
Managing payment plans.
Maintaining vendor invoices.
Coordinating vendor payments.
Tracking facility expenses.
Maintaining organized financial documentation.
Assisting with budget preparation and expense tracking.
Providing regular registration and revenue reports to leadership.

This position is not necessarily responsible for performing the organization’s accounting but should ensure that financial information is organized, accurate, and delivered to the appropriate accounting resources.
Uniforms, Equipment & Inventory

Coordinate uniform ordering and distribution.
Manage relationships with apparel and equipment vendors.
Maintain inventory of club equipment and supplies.
Track equipment issued to teams and coaches.
Coordinate equipment pickup and return.
Identify equipment needs before each season.
Ensure teams have necessary equipment prior to practices and games.

Seasonal Operations

Develop and manage a detailed operational calendar for each season.
This includes:
Pre-Season

Registration
Coach recruitment
Background checks
Team formation
Scheduling
Facility assignments
Uniform ordering
Equipment distribution
Parent communication
Coach communication

During the Season

Schedule management
Weather communication
Parent support
Coach support
Registration changes
Facility coordination
Equipment needs
Operational troubleshooting

Post-Season

Equipment collection
Financial reconciliation
Family surveys
Coach feedback
Registration reporting
Vendor reconciliation
Operational review
Recommendations for the following season

Technology & Systems

Manage and maintain the administrative systems used by the organization, which may include:
Registration software
Team-management applications
Scheduling software
Email systems
Website administration
Payment-processing platforms
QuickBooks or similar accounting systems
Google Workspace / Microsoft Office
Shared files and club databases

The Director should continually identify opportunities to automate repetitive administrative work and improve efficiency.
Policies & Risk Administration

Maintain participant waivers and required documentation.
Coordinate background checks and coach requirements.
Maintain insurance certificates and facility documentation.
Maintain organized electronic club records.
Assist leadership with implementing club policies and procedures.
Ensure administrative processes are consistently followed.

Events & Club Programming

Provide operational support for:
Opening-day events
Clinics
Camps
Tournaments
Picture days
Parent meetings
Coach meetings
Fundraising events
Community events
End-of-season activities

Leadership & Operational Management

The Director of Operations & Administration should operate as the central operational hub of the organization
.
Rather than leadership becoming involved in every scheduling issue, parent question, payment problem, uniform issue, or coach request, this individual should own those processes and escalate only issues requiring leadership decisions.
The Director will also help establish documented processes and operating procedures so the organization can continue to grow without creating unnecessary administrative complexity.
Key Performance Indicators

Performance should be measured using clear operational standards, including:
Registration accuracy
Response time to parent inquiries
Payment collection rate
Scheduling accuracy
Coach onboarding completion
Background-check compliance
Uniform delivery accuracy
Facility utilization
Number of unresolved parent/coach issues
Administrative cost per participant
Family satisfaction
Coach satisfaction

Qualifications

The ideal candidate will have:
3–5+ years of operations, administration, customer service, event management, or sports-management experience.
Strong organizational and project-management skills.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to manage hundreds of families and multiple teams simultaneously.
Strong attention to detail.
Experience working with registration or scheduling software.
Comfort working with spreadsheets, databases, and financial information.
Strong customer-service skills.
Ability to solve problems independently.
Willingness to work occasional evenings and weekends during peak periods.
Youth sports or recreational sports experience preferred.

Ideal Candidate Profile

We are looking for someone who is a highly organized operator and problem solver
.
This person should enjoy creating structure, building systems, communicating with families, and making sure hundreds of small operational details are completed correctly and on time.
They should be comfortable taking ownership rather than waiting for direction.
The successful candidate will constantly ask:
“What needs to happen next, who owns it, and how do we make sure it gets done?”

What Success Looks Like

Within the first year, this individual should create an operating environment where:
Families know exactly where to go for information.
Parent inquiries are answered quickly.
Coaches receive clear and timely communication.
Registrations and payments are accurately tracked.
Teams and schedules are organized well in advance.
Facilities are properly coordinated.
Uniforms and equipment arrive on time.
Leadership has accurate operational and financial reporting.
Administrative problems are solved before they become leadership problems.
The club has documented systems that can support continued growth beyond 1,000 participants.

Ultimately, the Director of Operations & Administration should allow club leadership to focus on strategy, programming, coaching quality, growth, partnerships, and the long-term direction of the organization
while this position owns the operational execution required to keep the club running successfully.
